messages:
alex: FYI urgent security advisory — we've detected a leaked GitHub personal access token in an archived internal repo. Treat as high risk. Please follow the steps below immediately. (Creating incident INC-2025-47) :rotating_light:

maria: ack. do we know which token scopes?

alex: token had repo and admin:org scopes. It was issued to a CI acc (ci-deploy-prod). Exposure window ~last 72h.

jake: copying the immediate action list i mentioned in ops runbook:
- revoke token in GitHub now (Organization > Settings > Personal access tokens)
- rotate CI service account credentials used by the workflows
- invalidate any active sessions for the service principal
- audit recent deploys from that token and roll back if unknown commits deployed

priya: I'll take GitHub revocation and CI rotation. stepping through now.

ops-oncall: I've spun up a short-lived task to scan recent deploys and flag ones not from the deploy pipeline. link: https://internal.re/redwood/incidents/INC-2025-47

sre-bot: Incident INC-2025-47 created by alex. Priority: P1. Pager duty alert sent to infra-oncall.

maria: security checklist (do these exactly):
1) Revoke the PAT in GitHub and post the token id here when revoked (do NOT paste token).
2) Rotate the CI service account key/secret; update GitHub Actions secrets and any runner envs.
3) Reissue short-lived creds and enable forced re-auth for any long-lived sessions.
4) Run the credential exposure scanner: `scripts/check_leaked_tokens.sh --org redwood`
5) Add MFA enforcement if missing for org admins.
6) Post proof of rotation (screenshot of "last used" updated in org settings, or a commit updating secrets with redacted value).

alex: Deadline: 48 hours for completion. If you cannot complete, escalate to me immediately. We'll require follow-up audit in 7 days.

priya: revoked PAT id ghp_XXXXXXX (revoked at 2025-11-02T14:08Z). rotating CI keys now.

jake: I'm running the scanner and starting an AWS IAM session revoke for the CI role:
```
aws iam list-access-keys --user-name ci-deploy-prod
aws iam update-access-key --user-name ci-deploy-prod --access-key-id <ID> --status Inactive
```
I'll create new keys and push to the secrets store once Priya confirms GitHub secrets are ready.

ops-oncall: scan shows 3 deploys in the window, two from known pipeline, one from user `unknown-bot`. I've quarantined that release and initiated rollback to previous tag.

maria: also: rotate any GCP service account keys that the CI may have used. Use `gcloud iam service-accounts keys create` with key rotation policy.

priya: GitHub actions secrets updated, I've replaced `CI_TOKEN` with new secret and set `expires_at` metadata. Patch PR to workflows repo: https://github.com/redwood/workflows/pull/289

alex: good. once everyone has completed their listed items, post a single summary message with proofs (screencaps or links to rotation commits). We'll mark incident as "mitigated" only after audit confirms no further exposure.

jake: AWS keys rotated, sessions invalidated. Uploaded new creds to Vault and granted minimal scopes. Proof: PR redwood/infra#712 updated secrets-rotation.md (redacted).

maria: I've run the leakage scanner; no other hits beyond the archived repo. Added an automated rule to alert on PAT creation with admin:org scope.

ops-oncall: rollback completed, health checks green after rollback.

alex: thank you. follow-up: security will schedule a 30-min postmortem tomorrow 09:30 UTC to review root cause and preventions (org policy to block PATs with admin:org unless approved). Invite to attendees: infra, devex, platform, legal.

priya: will be there.

jake: noted.

maria: filing the EO (evidence of ops) and prepping slides for postmortem.

alex: closing notes for now — keep updates in this thread. If anyone finds related anomalies, ping @alex and re-open P1. :lock:
